the reporter's own spelling

acceptance: A gate reading a tracked state-root file at the gated commit works for a nested state root on win32: the reported offset is forward-slashed and nothing rejoins it through `sep`.
tests: the pending gate reads the gated commit's queue under a backslash-separated state root
pins: computeStateRootRel reports a nested state root in git's alphabet
notes: `gitPath` (src/paths.ts) is the rule; `computeStateRootRel` (src/Dispatcher.ts:866) is the one reporter that never took it. The fixture shape is tests/harnessGates.test.ts's `NESTED` — a posix run cannot produce the offset, so it is spelled. src/friction.ts:191,221 compose the same value; check both.

edit.description: runGate records the throw's stack as that gate's details
the recorded details

summary: Record a thrown gate's stack as that gate's `details` — the details a returned refusal would have carried
acceptance: A gate that throws is recorded as `{ ok: false, message, details }`, and the failure the retry reads carries the stack rather than one line of message.
tests: a gate that throws records its stack as that gate's details
notes: `Dispatcher.runGate` (src/Dispatcher.ts:3657) already folds the throw to `{ ok: false, message }`; this is the `details` half of the amended sentence. A non-Error throw has no stack — what that records is build's call, stated at the site.

edit.description: one guard per hook seam, at the site both concurrencies share
all four legs

summary: Answer a throwing `promptArgs`, `shouldRun`, `handoff` or `shipped` the way its sibling seam already answers, never by losing the tick
acceptance: Each of the four hooks throwing lands on the outcome its seam already has, with the verdict written and the merge bookkeeping complete.
tests: a throwing promptArgs is a render-refused no-commit outcome
a throwing shouldRun refuses the tick rather than declining it
a throwing handoff is logged and the tick's facts stand
a throwing shipped leaves the entry pending and names the throw on the verdict
notes: Six unguarded call sites, four seams: src/Dispatcher.ts:1724 (handoff), 1849/3284 (shouldRun), 1967/3291 (promptArgs), 2888 (shipped). The singleton and fanout copies share one guard — `runGate` is the precedent (`.claude/rules/engineering.md`, *The fix lands at the mechanism*).

edit.description: `checkoutAt` beside the other git verbs
the detached checkout, placed under the worktree base
reclaim what a gate checked out, at the one gate-run site
placement and both reclamation legs

summary: Give a differential gate `api.git.checkoutAt` — a detached tree under the state root's worktree base, removed by the engine when the gate returns
acceptance: A gate needing the tree at `baseSha` asks the API for it and provisions nothing: the checkout lands under the worktree base and is gone when the gate returns, however it returns.
tests: api.git.checkoutAt plants a detached checkout under the state root's worktree base
the engine removes a gate's checkout when the gate returns
the engine removes a gate's checkout when the gate throws
notes: `Dispatcher.runGate` is the one gate-run site and so the one reclamation point. Under the worktree base, not a temp dir, so a run killed mid-flight leaves a directory the startup sweep reclaims. `harness/vitestRunner.ts`'s `runAtBase` is the standing hand-rolled checkout this replaces.

evaluate it at load against the resolved roots

the resolution order

summary: A chain may declare how to compute its worktree base — a function of the resolved roots, evaluated at load, never a committed path literal

per.section: Placement — the worktree base and the job namespace

acceptance: A chain declaring `worktreesBase` moves creation, per-wave stale-slug removal and the startup sweep together, without an environment variable set before the engine's own module loads.
tests: a chain-declared worktreesBase places the tick's worktree
the startup sweep reads the chain-declared base
notes: A function, not a path: placement stays machine-local, and a committed literal is the wrong home. The one computation stays `worktreesBase` (src/paths.ts) — a second is the defect field-traced four times. `harness/vitestRunner.ts` reads the same resolution.

edit.description: the base checkout comes from the api; its own worktree plumbing goes
the base run over an engine-supplied checkout

acceptance: `runAtBase` adds and removes no worktree of its own — the checkout is the API's and the engine reclaims it.
tests: runAtBase takes its base checkout from the engine's api rather than adding a worktree
notes: "A differential gate never provisions its own" is the ruling's second half; the named-lines judge is the differential gate and this runner is its only instance here. The `addWorktree`/`removeWorktree`/base-join block at harness/vitestRunner.ts:248-295 is what leaves.

acceptance: One porcelain record walk in the tree: the engine reports code and path with a rename or copy's origin field consumed, `trackedModifications` is its `??`-dropping filter, and the clean-tree gate spawns no git of its own.
tests: api.git reports a status record's code and path with a rename's origin field consumed
the clean-tree gate takes its status records from the engine rather than spawning git

The gate asks `--untracked-files=all`; the engine drops `??` either way, so one call at `all` serves both. gates.ts's module doc already claims no gate shells out.
